newsitem.title: LATVIA: MINISTER KRASTS ATTACKS PRIVATISATION AGENCY.
newsitem.headline: MINISTER KRASTS ATTACKS PRIVATISATION AGENCY.

text.p: Economy Minister Guntar Krasts on Friday said that he was not satisfied with the way the Latvian Privatisation Agency has sold off big companies and that he wanted an open competition to replace all four board members.
Krasts has already said that he wants two of the board members to replaced.
"The Latvian Privatisation Agency has shown great weakness in privatising large companies," Krasts told a news conference, explaining his opposition to the current board of directors.
"It would not be too late to change the board members as all the most important companies still await privatisation," he added.
"We have to organise a transparent competition, open for society, for all four board member posts," Krasts added.
Krasts has put himself in opposition to Prime Minister Andris Shkele over the board of the privatisation agency. Shkele has already said that the LPA board is not Krasts' business.
Newspapers have reported that Krasts in fact wants to put two colleagues from his Fatherland and Freedom party on the board of the LPA.
